runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Persisted sessions in disposable HOME and CODEX_HOME directories; generated Skill under project .agents/skills; user configuration and project rules ignored; gpt-6-astra parent with two fork_turns=none children; controlled stale replay through interrupt_agent and one followup_task call.
runtime.permissionProfile: Read-only sandbox with approval policy never

assertions.evidence: The parent received and read the generated check-stale-replay Skill before executing it.
Generation 1 invoked send_message to /root after its stale-asset read; the parent wait woke immediately and recorded an attributable MESSAGE from that child.
After the peer message arrived, a separate list_agents call reported generation_1 as running.
The parent invoked interrupt_agent only after the ready delivery and independent running-state check; the child's 120-second sleep was aborted.
The persisted parent transcript places the generation_2 spawn after the successful generation_1 interrupt acknowledgement.
Generation 2 read only fresh.txt and returned GENERATION=2 with FRESH_MARKER=fresh-ok before stale replay was requested; the parent retained that as the sole accepted result.
One followup_task targeted generation_1, and its original child JSONL contains the initial read turn plus a second turn in the same thread.
The resumed generation_1 thread returned GENERATION=1 and STALE_MARKER=late-generation-one-must-be-rejected without another file-read call.
The final result records ACCEPTED_GENERATION=2, ACCEPTED_MARKER=fresh-ok, STALE_PAYLOAD_RECEIVED=true, and STALE_RESULT_ACCEPTED=false.
The isolated Codex state directory contains one parent and exactly two child session JSONL files.
The final list_agents result reports both generation_1 and generation_2 completed with separately attributable payloads.
The parent read stale-replay-root-ok before child creation and independently read the same Skill-relative asset after both workers were terminal.
External post-run Git status reported no changes in the disposable probe repository.

limitations: This is a controlled replay: a follow-up deliberately releases a value retained before cancellation. It proves generation gating against a delivered stale payload, not a naturally racing post-cancellation network response.

Codex encrypts child assignment and peer-message bodies in persisted JSONL. The exact ready body is supported by the selected Skill contract, the child's send_message call, the attributable parent MESSAGE wake-up, and the final report rather than externally readable plaintext.
The parent first tried an incorrect repository-relative root path, then resolved and read the correct Skill-relative asset before creating any worker.
This is one passing model-mediated run; a repetition threshold is not yet established.
Unrelated installed MCP providers emitted authentication warnings during shutdown; the fixture used no MCP provider and completed successfully.
This evidence applies to Codex CLI only; desktop and IDE profiles remain unknown.
